newsitem.title: POLAND: Cross-border shoppers create tourism boom in Poland.
newsitem.headline: Cross-border shoppers create tourism boom in Poland.

text.p: The number of foreigners visiting Poland rose six percent to 87.5 million in 1996 and is likely to grow by nine percent this year, but the bulk of visitors were cross-border shoppers, the government's Physical Culture and Tourism Office said on Wednesday.
The office's deputy head Robert Kepinski said foreigners spent about $7 billion in Poland in 1996, up from $6.4 billion in 1995, mainly buying consumer products.
"Tourism is becoming increasingly important for our economy," Kepinski told a news conference.

But he said the number of "true" tourists, those who spent at least one night was much lower and amounted to 20.3 million last year, compared with 19.5 million in 1995. The remainder are one-day trippers doing shopping in Poland.

Kepinski said that according to the World Tourism Organisation statistics, Poland was ninth in the world in 1995 and 1996 in terms of the number of tourists visiting the country. It was 15th on the list of top tourism earners.
Poland saw a boom of foreign visitors after the fall of communism in 1989, when it liberalised its economy and travelling regulations.
In 1989, just eight million foreigners visited the country and the figure doubled annually in the next two years.
But analysts say that Poland needs to improve its underdeveloped tourist infrastructure and poor service quality to attract more holidaymakers.

Kepinski also said that the number of border crossings by Poles reached 44 million last year, compared with 37 million in 1995. The number of those who spent at least one night outside the country was nine million.
